title: Part 2 of my zombie game coded by Claude Opus 5.5
author: Silver-Chipmunk7744
selftext:
I was really impressed by a few things.  
First, it's the best char from scratch i ever seen an AI do. The priest looks great.

The pacing also generally feels really well done, the zombie models, the gunshot effects, the NPC behavior. For anyone who has tried to do similar projects with past models, this feels like a huge step up.

comments.author: orellanaed
comments.body: Godot + MCP? Or what's your setup?

replies.author: Silver-Chipmunk7744
replies.body:
None of those. Summary by Claude to make sure i am missing nothing.

>No Godot and no MCP. It's a browser game in plain JavaScript with three.js (a free 3D library). Claude Opus 5.5 writes all the code in Claude Code, about 60,000 lines so far. Everything is built by code: the characters, the church, the textures and the animations. Claude also tests the game itself: scripts it wrote run the game in a hidden Chrome window and take screenshots, so it can see what it made. The voices and sounds come from the ElevenLabs API, through a script Claude wrote. I play it, give feedback and decide what happens next.

One small caveat "Claude tested it itself" is not entirely true because i did give it feedback.

replies.author: orellanaed
replies.body: You should try Flockbay. You use your own Claude Code account and its Godot underneath but with better tools for AI game development

replies.author: Silver-Chipmunk7744
replies.body: Yeah I should definitely test godot at some point i saw nice outputs from it. I think its really good when your game has more complex physics?

replies.author: JorgitoEstrella
replies.body: The voice really seem human at least the ones from the girl, the animations were very stiff though.

replies.author: Silver-Chipmunk7744
replies.body:
Well the voices are the newest Eleven lab V4 voices, i also think they're great.

Which animations do you refer to? All of them?

I agree with you, but remember this is all made from scratch. I did not give Claude any rigged characters. So honestly, in my opinion those animations are way better than what we had from previous models, but yeah you are correct and they're still not as good as those from real games.

It would probably be possible to spend more time telling Claude which animations to improve.

replies.author: JorgitoEstrella
replies.body:
Yeah seems that AI still cannot do well animations/rigging so you will have to do it manually.

Really impressive by the AI voices, now they seem to have some emotion.

replies.author: Silver-Chipmunk7744
replies.body: Yes and interestingly, i let Claude handle the voice creation on it's own. It was adding the tags and so on to make it more interesting.

comments.author: Imnotanad
comments.body: So ElevenLabs can produce spatial audio ?

replies.author: Silver-Chipmunk7744
replies.body:
Huhhh i don't think so. Let me ask Claude since i'm jus the silly human who doesn't know how this works:  
\_\_\_

The voice files from ElevenLabs have no direction. Each one is a flat mono (single-channel) sound. The game adds the direction while it plays the line.

**How it works**

1. **The sound starts at the mouth.** When Akane or the priest speaks, the game places the line at their head in the 3D world.
2. **A "3D ear" filter.** The browser's sound system (Web Audio) sends the voice through an HRTF filter. HRTF is a recipe for how a real head and real ears change a sound that comes from each direction. The sound reaches one ear a tiny bit earlier, and the shape of the ear changes its tone. Your brain reads these clues as a direction: left, right, front or back.
3. **Your ears follow the camera.** Every frame, the game tells the sound system where you are and which way you look. When you turn, the voice moves to the other ear.
4. **Distance.** Farther away is quieter. The voices fade slowly with distance, so a far call stays clear.
5. **Room echo.** Some of each voice goes into an echo made by code. It is 2.4 seconds of soft noise that dies away, like a big room. The priest gets the most echo, because he is in a church. Akane gets a little.
6. **Sara has no position.** Her voice plays in the middle of your head, with almost no echo, because it is "your" voice. Next to her, the other voices feel like they are outside you.
